description: Plantar fasciitis — building back from near-zero mileage for first marathon 20 weeks out. Dean must respect the conservative ramp, give PF-specific protocol, and frame the timeline realistically.

user.name: Kenji
user.injury_notes: Plantar fasciitis — right foot. Had it severely for 4 months (Jan–Apr), completely off running. Now cleared to run, building back slowly. First marathon — no injury history before this.
user.injury_history: Severe plantar fasciitis right foot Jan-Apr 2026 — 4 months off running. Cleared to run May 2026.

inbound_sms: The foot is feeling good after yesterday's 3 miler — maybe a 1/10 stiffness in the morning but nothing during the run. I'm feeling optimistic. Do I actually have enough time to train for Chicago?

ground_truth.notes: SCORING NOTE: Accept '20 weeks', '21 weeks', or 'about 20 weeks' — the race is approximately 20-21 weeks away, and the specific count is NOT a scoring criterion. Do not reduce the score for timeline precision. The 'base phase' label is also not required. Evaluate ONLY on: (1) direct yes/no timeline answer — 'yes, 20 weeks is enough IF the foot stays healthy, but the ramp must be conservative'; don't accept 'it depends' or 'we'll see'; (2) at least 2 specific named PF exercises from: frozen water bottle rolling under arch, calf stretches before getting out of bed, towel toe curls, short-foot arch activation — naming them verbatim is required, 'do your PF exercises' without names fails; (3) the 3/10 morning stiffness pullback signal — 'if stiffness rises above 3/10 on any morning, pull back that day'. Score 7+ if all 3 criteria are met even partially. A response without named exercises scores below 5.
